what_changed.text: Oil drops from $112 to $96 — a 14% decline over three weeks. The Oil/SPR Capacity Ratio falls from 270 to 231, but the score holds at 2. The drop removes some immediate price pressure, but it doesn't restore the SPR circuit breaker. Refilling the reserve at $96 would still cost over $40B, and the political will doesn't exist. The underlying vulnerability remains.

DXY breaks below 100 for the first time this cycle — now at 98.7. The dollar lost the psychological 100 floor while gold held above $4,700. Dollar weakness alongside persistent gold strength is precisely the monetary divergence this framework was built to detect.

S&P recovers against gold: ratio rises from 1.40 to 1.51. Equities gained nominally while gold held roughly flat. Tier 3 score drops from 4 to 3 as S&P/Gold crosses back below the scoring threshold. The framework records short-term moves accurately — one period of equity outperformance is noted, not dismissed.

Scores settle at T1=3/10, T2=6/20, T3=3/12. Status: Emerging Disorder — Elevated. The structural indicators remain at maximum readings. Gold's 8-week momentum weakened again to -8.6%, but the annual trend (+44% YoY) is intact. The framework hasn't escalated — and the raw data hasn't given it reason to de-escalate either.

contrarian: Oil fell 14% and everyone called it a reprieve. The Canary isn't buying it. At $96, refilling the SPR to pre-2022 levels would still cost over $100B and take years to execute. The 2022 release required drawing 180M barrels at $120 — that intervention stabilized markets temporarily. Now the reserve sits at 415M barrels (58% capacity), and the political will to refill it doesn't exist at any price. The circuit breaker isn't broken because oil is too expensive. It's broken because the reserve isn't full. A drop to $96 doesn't fix that.

The dollar broke 100 and nobody wrote about it. DXY at 98.7 is not noise — 100 has been the psychological floor for dollar reserve status in this cycle. Gold sat at $4,729 the same week. When the dollar weakens and gold holds, that is the divergence the framework was built to detect. The financial press spent the week writing about oil. The Canary is watching the dollar.

The S&P 'recovered' against gold this week. The ratio moved from 1.40 to 1.51. But zoom out: the S&P/Gold ratio peaked near 2.5 in late 2021. It now sits at 1.51 — meaning equities have surrendered roughly 40% of their purchasing power in gold terms over four years. One good week doesn't change the structural direction. The framework records it accurately. It doesn't change the interpretation.

divergence.description: The single most predictive indicator in The Canary. When gold surges and yields don't follow, the bond market is being artificially suppressed — either through direct purchases or implicit policy. This divergence preceded every major regime transition in the last 50 years.
divergence.current_reading: Current reading: Gold +44% YoY while 10Y yields are flat to slightly lower. The divergence remains extreme even as gold's 8-week momentum is negative — annual trends don't reverse in weeks. DXY breaking below 100 while this divergence persists is the framework's core signal: the dollar is weakening, gold is holding, and bond yields are being suppressed. The gap between gold and yields remains one of the widest sustained divergences in modern monetary history. The bond market is telling you everything is fine. The gold market and the dollar are telling you something else.

consensus.wall_street: Supply normalization — OPEC+ responding, demand concerns easing. Energy price pressure is behind us.
consensus.atlas: The SPR is still at 58% capacity. At $96, refilling costs $40B+. The circuit breaker that worked in 2022 is still unavailable. The score holds at 2 because the underlying vulnerability — not the oil price — is what the indicator measures.

consensus.wall_street: Minor pullback in a strong dollar trend. DXY below 100 is temporary.
consensus.atlas: First break of 100 this cycle. Gold at $4,729 simultaneously. Dollar weakness + gold strength is the monetary divergence signal — not noise. The 8wk DXY trend is still positive but decelerating fast.

consensus.wall_street: S&P at 7138 confirms the bull market is intact. Gold was the overreaction.
consensus.atlas: S&P/Gold at 1.51 vs the 2021 peak of ~2.5. Equities are up nominally, but down 40% in gold terms over 4 years. One week of outperformance is recorded accurately by the framework — it doesn't change the 4-year trend.
Balance sheet now growing at 1.8% over 3 months — faster than last reading of +0.5%. Direction matters more than rate level. The stealth expansion continues.

consensus.atlas: Holding at 2.40% for a second consecutive reading. The widening trend from 2.17% stalled — watch for direction over the next 2-3 weeks.
TC/RCs at $0 says smelters are in crisis. Headline inventory masks geographic dislocation and tariff front-loading.

positioning.intro: Emerging Disorder — Elevated holds, but the composition shifted. Oil's retreat and equity recovery pulled Tier 3 down by one point. The framework records this accurately — short-term mean reversion is real and worth tracking. But the structural indicators haven't moved: copper smelters are still paying miners, silver deficits are compounding, and the Fed's balance sheet is growing faster than last month. The dollar just broke 100. Position for the structure, not the noise.

posture.label: Gold — overweight
posture.reason: Holding at $4,729 with DXY breaking below 100. YoY +44% with 8-week momentum negative at -8.6% — the same pattern as the April 2 reading. Annual divergence with yields remains extreme. Dollar weakness adds a second tailwind the framework hadn't fully priced in.

posture.label: Bitcoin — overweight
posture.reason: Functions as high-beta gold in monetary regime transitions. DXY breaking 100 while gold holds is the setup BTC correlates with most strongly. Position size for volatility.

posture.label: Short-term Treasuries — hold
posture.reason: T-bills under 1-year maturity. Dry powder for deployment if the coiling pattern breaks toward escalation. Eliminated at Crisis Acceleration when Treasuries themselves become the problem.

posture.label: Critical materials — overweight
posture.reason: Copper TC/RCs still at $0 (score 2), silver deficit at 800M oz cumulative (score 2), oil/SPR ratio at 231 (score 2). All three supply-side indicators at maximum. Oil's drop to $96 didn't change the SPR vulnerability score — the reserve is still at 58% capacity.

posture.label: Equities — underweight
posture.reason: S&P/Gold ratio recovered to 1.51 from the 1.40 low — the framework records this. But the 4-year trend shows equities have lost ~40% of their purchasing power in gold terms since 2021. Nominal gains masking real losses.

posture.label: Long Treasuries — underweight
posture.reason: Dollar breaking 100 while yields remain suppressed adds a new dimension to the risk. The Gold/Treasury Divergence says yields are artificially pinned. With the dollar now weakening, the case for long-duration bonds deteriorates further.

escalation: Gold 8-week momentum recovers above +10% → Gold Momentum returns to Score 2 and Tier 1 re-escalates. Currently at -8.6% — the window has widened since last reading.

Fed shifts to long-duration purchases while The Canary reads Early Warning or above → immediate Crisis Acceleration (Override Rule #4). QE launched from Stable does not trigger — it's a crisis response, not a cause.
Treasury auction B/C drops below 2.0 → demand crisis signal. Currently masked by Fed purchases — watch what happens if they pause.

Tier 2 confirming score reaches ≥8 → triggers Transition via combined T1+T2 gate. Currently at 6/20. DXY breaking 100 is a warning — if credit spreads widen further or foreign holdings drop, the path to 8 shortens.
deescalation: Gold YoY drops below +30% while yields rise → genuine tightening. Currently at +44% — above this threshold but the gap is narrowing from the +50% peak.
Fed resumes QT at full pace → balance sheet contracting. Not just slowing purchases — actively shrinking. Balance sheet is currently growing faster than last month.
Tier 1 drops to 0–2 (currently 3/10) → returns to Stable. Would require gold momentum AND divergence to normalize simultaneously.
Deficit/GDP falls below 5% → structural fiscal pressure easing. Currently at 5.8% and rising.

track_record.intro: Applied retroactively across nine historical periods, The Canary identified every major regime transition 3–6 months early with near-zero false positives.

adversarial.label: Gold rally (+25%)
adversarial.result: No signal ✔ — cyclical bounce with no yield divergence or Fed expansion. Gold reversed within a year.

adversarial.label: Gold bear market (−45%)
adversarial.result: No false signal ✔ — real tightening with rising yields. The system correctly read this as non-monetary.

adversarial.label: Fed tightening cycle
adversarial.result: No false signal ✔ — QT was running and balance sheet shrinking. No divergence to trigger on.

adversarial.label: LTCM / Russia crisis
adversarial.result: Correctly filtered ✔ — financial stress but no monetary regime implications. Fed cut rates and markets stabilized.

adversarial.label: SVB banking stress
adversarial.result: Brief signal, self-corrected ✔ — initial spike in Fed lending resolved within weeks. No sustained monetary shift.

adversarial.label: 30-year balance sheet expansion
adversarial.result: Right on direction, open on timing — BOJ's experiment is still running. The framework flags the trajectory correctly but can't call the endpoint.
